decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “save a link, have it become readable automatically, then find and reopen it later.” R2 client confirms the direction; R5 later confirms the row opens the actual website.
decisions.note: Conforming high-level core journey, with the reopening clarification linked to its eventual conforming disposition.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker places “Labels, search, read-later, archiving, editing details, and duplicate handling” in scope; R2 client says she is glad they are on the radar.
decisions.note: Conforming early scope framing; concrete behavior is reviewed in later decisions.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents one prominent Save link button that “only asks for the web address.” R4 client confirms she pasted only the address and saved.
decisions.note: Conforming save-by-URL decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker specifies automatic presentation of “page icon, title, short description, and website name” but no preview image. R4 client approves that enumerated field set without mentioning the missing preview image.
decisions.note: Prototype metadata decision omits REF-BM-02’s required preview image; the response does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents a readable result with icon, title, description, and website name; R4 client says it is recognizable rather than a wall of raw links.
decisions.note: Conforming readability-first list presentation; tags are added in a later decision.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker’s first save flow goes from URL directly to the readable item. R4 client asks whether she can “fix up the title or description… both right when I save and later on.”
decisions.note: During prototype review, the client requests the related before-save and later-edit requirements missing from the presented first flow.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker states “the whole bookmark row opens the actual recipe page, not an information page.” R5 client tests it and confirms the actual page opened.
decisions.note: Conforming original-URL navigation after the R4 clarification.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker recaps saving from a URL, readable page details, and opening the real website; R6 client explicitly confirms all three.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype checkpoint.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker presents fetching details, pausing for review, and editing title and description before save. R7 client confirms both fields were editable and retained.
decisions.note: Conforming edit-before-save decision.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker specifies that details appear automatically, either field may be changed or left untouched, and the saved bookmark still opens the original site. R8 client confirms the complete behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming save-review behavior.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presents later editing of title and description through a separate visible Edit control. R9 client successfully changes both fields.
decisions.note: Conforming later edit for title and description.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker says the website address was kept unchanged in this edit. R9 client asks that “the same edit include changing the address” when a link is wrong or moves.
decisions.note: The client extends the presented later-edit scope to the URL field required by REF-BM-04.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker presents URL correction that preserves custom text, updates the site name, and opens the new address. R10 client confirms all of those outcomes.
decisions.note: Conforming revised URL-edit decision.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presents selecting Recipes in the sidebar to narrow the collection to recipe bookmarks. R11 client confirms the tag-only filter.
decisions.note: Conforming specific-tag filtering.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presents filtering an example collection by existing labels. R11 client asks how to assign labels and whether one bookmark can carry more than one.
decisions.note: The client requests missing assignment and multi-tag behavior from the presented label scope.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker presents existing label filters but no entry interaction. R11 client says typing an existing label should suggest it to prevent near-duplicates.
decisions.note: The client explicitly extends the label workflow with required autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker presents selecting Work and Recipes and saving both on one bookmark. R12 client confirms both chips and both updated filter counts.
decisions.note: Conforming multiple-tag assignment.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker instructs typing partial label names and choosing suggested existing labels. R12 client confirms Work and Recipes were suggested.
decisions.note: Conforming existing-tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker presents removing Recipes while retaining Work. R13 client confirms only the selected tag disappeared.
decisions.note: Conforming tag editing/removal.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker exhaustively says search checks “titles, descriptions, website names, addresses, and labels,” omitting bookmark notes. R14 client discusses those fields but does not surface note search.
decisions.note: The presented full-text field coverage omits notes required by REF-BM-12; this also reflects the absent note capability in REF-BM-23.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker presents basic live search. R14 client asks that CREAMY and Creamy return the same result because search should ignore capitalization.
decisions.note: The client requests the missing case-insensitive rule.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker presents labels among ordinary searched fields. R14 client requests a way to search specifically by a label rather than mix it with text.
decisions.note: The client catches the missing tag-specific search capability, though she does not state the reference’s required #tag syntax.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker presents a plain-word search. R14 client asks to search “a few words in a row” as exact wording.
decisions.note: The client requests missing exact-phrase behavior.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker presents a single-term search. R14 client asks to combine searches such as “potatoes but not the carrot one” and “recipes or work.”
decisions.note: The client requests missing boolean-combination semantics from the presented search scope.

decisions.evidence: R15 maker asks the client to replace creamy with CREAMY and retain the same result. R15 client confirms it.
decisions.note: Conforming case-insensitive search.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker presents tag search as `label:recipes`. R16 client says that form is understandable and flags only an unrelated screenshot mismatch; she never identifies the required `#tag` syntax.
decisions.note: The prototype uses `label:` instead of REF-BM-14’s specified `#tag` syntax, and the response does not surface that reference difference.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker presents `"creamy centers"` as an exact phrase. R17 client confirms only the contiguous phrase matches.
decisions.note: Conforming quoted-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker presents exclusion with `-carrot`. R18 client says the minus sign feels natural but does not identify that REF-BM-15 requires the `NOT` operator.
decisions.note: The exclusion notation departs from the required NOT syntax; approval of the shown form does not itself surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: R19 maker presents `label:recipes OR label:work`; R19 client confirms either side is included. Her screenshot correction does not alter the conforming live OR behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming OR semantics during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker presents adjacency—`potatoes label:recipes`—as implicit AND and says OR is required only to widen. R20 client explicitly states that putting them beside one another should mean both match, calls that exactly what she expects, and accepts it.
decisions.note: The client explicitly adopts implicit conjunction instead of REF-BM-15’s required AND-operator form, so this is an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker presents a one-click Read later control and a separate Read later sidebar view. R21 client confirms the marked item appears there alone.
decisions.note: Conforming unread marking and unread-only view.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker presents adding an item to Read later but not clearing it. R21 client asks to mark it read so it drops from that list.
decisions.note: The client requests the missing mark-read half of the workflow.

decisions.evidence: R22 maker presents Mark as read removing only Read later status while preserving the bookmark in All bookmarks. R22 client confirms that behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming mark-read behavior.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker presents archiving as hiding an item from All bookmarks without deleting it and making it visible in Archive. R23 client confirms both outcomes.
decisions.note: Conforming archive and archive-only list behavior.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker states only that archiving hides the item from All bookmarks. R23 client adds that archived items must also stay out of normal search and appear only in Archive.
decisions.note: The client requests the missing ordinary-search exclusion rule for archived bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker presents reversible archive behavior. R23 client asks for a separate delete that “actually remove[s] the bookmark permanently, not just tuck[s] it away.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing permanent-delete behavior and archive/delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: R24 maker presents an archived item being absent from All-bookmarks search and appearing when the same search is viewed in Archive. R24 client confirms both.
decisions.note: Conforming archived-search scope.

decisions.evidence: R25 maker presents an irreversible confirmed delete that leaves Archive empty. R25 client confirms the item is permanently gone and distinguishes it from archive.
decisions.note: Conforming permanent deletion and archive/delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: R26 maker presents Restore returning the same bookmark unchanged rather than creating a copy. R26 client confirms its title, description, and site are preserved.
decisions.note: Conforming reversible archive restoration.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker presents duplicate detection before creation, keeping the count unchanged and moving to the highlighted existing item. R27 client confirms it points her to the bookmark already saved.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate convergence; the existing row has the previously established visible Edit control.

decisions.evidence: R28 maker presents rejecting `not a link`, preserving the input, and creating no bookmark. R28 client confirms she can correct the URL in place.
decisions.note: Conforming enforcement of the required URL field.

decisions.evidence: R29 maker presents a valid URL remaining saveable when metadata retrieval fails, with manually supplied text and a neutral icon. R29 client confirms the bookmark is saved and still opens the address.
decisions.note: Conforming fallback around automatic metadata failure; the separate title-required departure is presented explicitly in R32.

decisions.evidence: R31 maker presents deliberately creating a new Planning tag only after Enter while existing tags remain suggestions. R31 client confirms that prevents accidental near-duplicates.
decisions.note: Conforming tag creation alongside autocomplete-based reuse.

decisions.evidence: R32 maker requires a nonempty title and allows an empty description. R32 client explicitly states “a title is required and a description is optional,” says this matches how she thinks, and accepts it.
decisions.note: The client explicitly accepts a departure from the reference entity rule and REF-BM-01, under which URL is the required field and saving is possible by entering the URL.

decisions.evidence: R33 maker presents stripping recognizable tracking parameters for duplicate comparison and preserving the cleaner saved URL. R33 client confirms no duplicate is created.
decisions.note: Conforming strengthening of duplicate convergence.

decisions.evidence: R34 maker presents compact truncation in the list while Edit preserves complete title and description text. R34 client confirms the list remains readable and no data is lost.
decisions.note: Conforming readability-first display with full editable values.

decisions.evidence: R38 maker states that an unavailable external page never causes automatic removal and that only the user may correct, archive, or delete it. R38 client explicitly confirms that control.
decisions.note: Conforming user-controlled removal and archive/delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: R40 maker presents the implemented app as passing all twenty approved scenarios. R40 client reports testing readable saves, opening, editing, labeling, searching, Read later, archive, and persistence, then accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: Implementation-review confirmation of the reference-conforming portions of the approved scope; known syntax and metadata departures are classified separately.

decisions.evidence: R40 maker presents the real app as ready for acceptance. R40 client explicitly identifies “jotting my own notes on a bookmark” as something still wanted later, says it is “for another day,” and accepts the app without it.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client surfaces and explicitly defers the absent bookmark-note capability.

decisions.evidence: R40 maker presents the real app as ready for acceptance. R40 client explicitly identifies “bringing in the bookmarks I already have elsewhere” as a future need, says it does not hold up acceptance, and accepts.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client surfaces and explicitly defers bookmark import; the response does not specify Netscape details, but clearly accepts absence of the broader required import capability.
